Motor/drive temperature. NO physical temperature sensor on this hardware (see DATASET_ISSUES.md [2026-06-06]); supplied as an I^2R thermal estimate from current, the same way load_torque_est_nm is estimated from current. Required as an MPC plant state and an LSTM anomaly feature. NOTE: measured_or_derived stays "measured" here in the historian sense — temp_c is INGESTED as an external input (it is NOT produced by the derive_signals step, which is what "derived" means in this pipeline). Its estimated origin is recorded via quality_flag_default=2 (derived_or_estimated) and the thermal_estimate_i2r source_method, not via the schema's measured/derived enum. See DECISION_LOG.md [2026-06-06].

Electrical input power = voltage_v * current_a. This is precisely what the INA219 power register (INA_mW) reports: profiling the acquisition file showed that register is the on-chip product of the bus-voltage and current registers (median relative error 0.26%), not an independent measurement. It is therefore computed rather than ingested, so the model is not fed the same information twice under two names.
Mechanical shaft power = load_torque_est_nm * speed_rpm * 2*pi/60. Together with power_w it separates "drawing current and doing work" from "drawing current and doing nothing" (a jam).

Drivetrain efficiency estimate = clip(mech_power_w / power_w, 0, 1). Clipped because values above 1 are physically impossible and would only signal torque-estimate drift. A collapse toward 0 while power_w stays high is the signature of a stalled or jammed belt.
Angular acceleration = speed_delta_rpm / dt, with dt measured from consecutive sample timestamps. Rate-normalised so the feature stays valid if the logger period changes.

LEAKY accumulation of tracking_error_rpm * dt — the observable proxy for the PID integral term. A sustained non-zero value means the loop cannot reach its target (slipping belt, jam, supply sag), which a single-sample error cannot reveal. The leak (exp(-dt/error_integral_tau_s)) is essential, not cosmetic: tracking error on a loaded conveyor has a persistent non-zero mean, so a plain sum is a drifting random walk that runs to its clamp and stays there — measured at 93.7% of samples pinned on the first build, i.e. a constant. With the leak, steady state under a constant error e is e*tau, so the feature measures how badly and how persistently the loop is missing. error_integral_clamp_s * rated_speed_rpm remains as a hard backstop.
Tracking error normalised by commanded speed: 100 * tracking_error_rpm / max(|setpoint_rpm|, 1). Makes a 20 RPM error at 330 RPM and at 660 RPM comparable.

Apparent load resistance = voltage_v / max(current_a, 1e-4). Rises toward an open circuit (broken winding / lost connection) and falls toward a short. Complements power_w because it is a ratio rather than a product.
power_w[t] - power_w[t-1] — electrical power transient.

Headroom to the configured limit = max_safe_temp_c - temp_c. NOTE: this is an audit/telemetry signal only. It does NOT make the safety envelope enforce a temperature limit — that remains unwired, see OPEN_QUESTIONS #31.
Headroom to the configured limit = max_safe_current_a - current_a. Audit / telemetry signal; the hard current block lives in safety_envelope.py.
